topic: housing subscription (cheongyak): new apartments allotted by points and lottery
title: In Korea, a New Home Is Something You Win

slides.headline: In Korea, a new home is **something you win.**
slides.note: Points, luck, and a savings account.

slides.headline: It's called **cheongyak**
slides.body: 청약, an application to buy a new apartment before it's even built. Most new apartments are sold this way.

slides.headline: First, **the account**
slides.body: You need a housing subscription savings account. About half the country holds one. Some parents open it for their kids.

slides.headline: Points for **waiting**
slides.body: Years without a home, more dependents, an older account. 84 points is the maximum. The longer you wait, the higher you rank.

slides.headline: Or a **straight draw**
slides.body: Some units skip the points and go by random lottery. Luck instead of years.

slides.headline: Seats **set aside**
slides.body: Newlyweds, first-time buyers, families with many kids and new parents each get their own share of the units.

slides.headline: Why **everyone applies**
slides.body: In some areas the price is capped below the market. Win, and you can be ahead on day one. People call it a lotto.

slides.headline: Applications for **one apartment**
slides.body: One leftover unit near Seoul in 2024, sold at its 2017 price. The application site slowed to a crawl.

slides.headline: Elsewhere you make an offer. **Here, you apply.**
slides.body: In many countries buyers bid against each other. In Korea, a points table and a draw set the line.

slides.headline: Korea, explained **by a Korean.**
slides.body: Follow for the context behind the things Korea does.
slides.graphic: New apartment towers under construction near Seoul at dusk, softly blurred behind the text.

caption:
In Korea, most new apartments aren't bought. They're won.

You apply with a savings account, then points for years without a home, or a random draw, decide who gets one.

How do people buy a new home where you live?
reply: One more: winning comes with strings. In the hottest areas you can't resell for years, and a winner can be barred from applying again for up to 10 years. Since late 2024, up to ₩250,000 a month counts toward the account. Would a points-and-lottery system for homes work where you live?
fact_check: 2장: 청약 = 분양 아파트 입주자 모집에 신청. 선분양 관행(착공 시 분양). 주택공급에 관한 규칙.
3장: 주택청약종합저축 가입자 약 2,600만 명대(2024~2025, 인구 약 5,100만의 절반). 미성년자 가입 가능(미성년 기간 최대 5년 인정, 2024 개정).
4장: 민영주택 가점제 84점 만점 = 무주택기간 32 + 부양가족수 35 + 청약통장 가입기간 17.
5장: 추첨제 — 면적·지역별로 일부 물량 추첨(85㎡ 초과 비중 큼).
6장: 특별공급 — 신혼부부, 생애최초, 다자녀, 노부모부양, 신생아(2024~) 등.
7장: 분양가상한제 적용 지역은 시세보다 낮게 분양 → '로또 청약' 표현. 'can'으로 표기.
8장: 2024-07 화성 동탄역 롯데캐슬 무순위(줍줍) 1가구에 294만여 명 신청, 2017년 분양가 그대로. 청약홈 접속 지연·마비 보도.
9장: 일반화 — 다수 국가는 매도자와 가격 협상·경매식. 특정국 단정 안 함.
댓글: 전매제한(지역별 최대 수년), 재당첨 제한 최대 10년(투기과열·분상제). 2024-11-01부터 월 납입 인정액 10만→25만원.
